(December 2025){{Cite web |title=Telecom Subscription Reports |url=https://trai.gov.in/release-publication/reports/telecom-subscriptions-reports |website=TELECOM REGULATORY AUTHORITY OF INDIA}} | num_employees = 51,145 (as on 30 June 2024, as per RTI) | founded = {{start date and age|df=yes|2000|10|01}} | founder = [[Government of India]] | hq_location_city = [[New Delhi]] | hq_location_country = India | website = {{URL|https://bsnl.co.in}} }} '''Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited''' ({{Translation|'''India Telecom Corporation Limited'''}}), commonly known as BSNL is an Indian [[Public Sector Undertakings in India|central public sector undertaking]], under the [[ownership]] of [[Department of Telecommunications]]. It was established on 1st October 2000 by the Government of India. It provides mobile voice and internet services through its nationwide [[Telecommunications in India|telecommunications]] network across India. It is the largest [[List of telecom companies in India|government-owned-wireless telecommunications service provider]] in India.{{cite web|url=https://main.trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/PR_No.09of2020.pdf|title=Press Release on Telecom Subscription Data as on 30 November, 2019|date=30 November 2019|website=Telecom Regulatory Authority of India|access-date=16 January 2020|archive-date=29 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200229013323/https://main.trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/PR_No.09of2020.pdf|url-status=dead}} ==History== [[File:BSNL New Logo.png|alt=BSNL Old logo|thumb|BSNL logo used until October 2024]] Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited is an Indian [[Government of India|government enterprise]] and its history can be traced back to [[British Raj]]. The foundation of the telecommunications network in India was laid by the British sometime during the 19th century. During the British era, the first telegraph line was established between [[Kolkata]] and Diamond Harbour in 1850. The British [[East India Company]] started using the telegraph in 1851, and by 1854, telegraph lines were laid across the country. In 1854, the telegraph service was opened to the public, and the first telegram was sent from Mumbai to Pune. In 1885, the [[Indian Telegraph Act, 1885|Indian Telegraph Act]] was passed by the [[Imperial Legislative Council|British Imperial Legislative Council]]. After the bifurcation of the Post and Telegraph department in the 1980s, the creation of [[Department of Telecommunications|Department of Telecom]] eventually led to the emergence of the [[Government of India|government owned telegraph and telephone enterprise]], which led to the foundation of BSNL.{{cite news|url=https://www.bsnl.co.in/opencms/bsnl/BSNL/about_us/company/about_bsnl.html|title=About us|date=17 November 2019|publisher=BSNL, LLC}} Until the early 2000s, BSNL was the only service provider for [[Indian Railways]] to control and administrative communication circuits. Later, they were separated as [[RailTel]]. For 160 years, BSNL had operated the public telegram service. In 2010, the telex network between its 182 offices was replaced with the "Web-Based Telegram Messaging System" which relied on internet connections rather than telex lines (which are more reliable where power outages are more common). This led to a decline in service, and the company applied the title "diminished service" to telegrams in 2010. Finally, on 15 July 2013, the public telegram service was shut down completely.{{cite news |title = BSNL decides to discontinue 160-year-old telegram service | url = https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/BSNL-decides-to-discontinue-160-year-old-telegram-service/articleshow/20554017.cms | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130615032137/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-06-12/india/39924887_1_telegram-telegraph-offices-telecom-employees | url-status = live | archive-date = 15 June 2013 | date = 12 June 2013 |work = [[The Times of India]] | access-date = 13 June 2013 }}{{cite news | last = Joshi| first = Sandeep| title = Dot, dash, full stop: Telegram service ends July 15 | url = http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/bsnl-to-shut-down-telegram-services-from-june-15/article4806921.ece | work = The Hindu | date = 12 June 2013 | access-date = 13 June 2013 | location = Chennai, India}} BSNL also enjoys a part of revenue from the payments made for private players for recharge plans. ==Products and services== ===Telephone and Mobile=== BSNL provides both [[landline|fixed line telephones]] and [[mobile telephony]] services on the [[GSM]] platform. ====BSNL Mobile==== {{main|BSNL Mobile}} [[BSNL Mobile]] is a major provider of [[GSM]] network services under the brand names ''CellOne'' and BSNL all over India. It has a wide network coverage in both urban and rural areas of India. It has over 121.82 million customers across India. BSNL Mobile offers [[prepaid mobile phone|prepaid]], [[Postpaid mobile phone|postpaid]] services and value-added services such as Free Phone Service (FPS), India Telephone Card (Prepaid card), Account Card Calling (ACC), [[Virtual private network|Virtual Private Network]] (VPN), Tele-voting, Premium Rate Service (PRM). It also offers the [[Internet Protocol television|IPTV]], which enables customers to watch television through the Internet and Voice and Video Over Internet Protocol (VVoIP).{{cite web |url=http://www.techtree.com/India/News/BSNL_Launches_VVOIP/551-115563-613.html |title=BSNL Launches VVoIP |publisher=Techtree.com |access-date=17 September 2012 |archive-date=13 December 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111213170642/http://www.techtree.com/India/News/BSNL_Launches_VVOIP/551-115563-613.html |url-status=dead }} ====BSNL Landline==== BSNL Landline was launched in the early 1990s. It was the only fixed-line telephone service for the whole country before the New Telecom Policy was announced by the [[Department of Telecommunications|Department of Telecom]] in 1999. Only the Government-owned BSNL and MTNL were allowed to provide land-line phone services through [[Copper conductor|copper wire]] in the country. BSNL Landline is the [[List of telecom companies in India#Wireline operators|largest fixed-line telephony]] in India. It has over 9.55 million customers and 47.20% market share in the country as of 28 February 2021. ===Internet=== BSNL is the [[List of telecom companies in India#Internet service providers (ISPs)|fourth-largest ISP]] in India, having a presence throughout the country. It also has the largest Firebase telecom network in the country, around 7.5 lakh kilometers, among the four operators in the country.{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/telecom-news/lacking-government-support-bsnl-plans-to-monetise-fibre-network/articleshow/68934188.cms|title=BSNL plans to monitise fibre network|date=18 April 2019|publisher=[[The Economic Times]]}} ====BSNL Broadband==== {{main|BSNL Broadband}} BSNL Broadband provides telecom services to enterprise customers, including MPLS, [[Peer-to-peer|P2P]] and Internet leased lines. It provides fixed-line services and landlines using [[Code-division multiple access|CDMA]] technology and its own extensive optical fiber network. BSNL provides [[Internet access]] services through dial-up connections as prepaid, ''NetOne'' as postpaid, and ''DataOne'' as [[BSNL Broadband]].[http://bsnl.co.in/service/dataone.htm BSNL Broadband] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091124192915/http://bsnl.co.in/service/dataone.htm |date=24 November 2009 }}{{Cite web|url=http://www.netone.in/service/internet_typeofaccess.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090503112723/http://www.netone.in/service/internet_typeofaccess.htm#cli|url-status=dead|title=Netone.in|archive-date=3 May 2009|website=Netone.in|access-date=17 July 2026}} ==== BSNL Bharat Fiber ==== BSNL Bharat Fiber ([[Fiber to the x|FTTH]]) was launched in February 2019. It offers [[Internet Protocol television|TV over IP (IPTV)]], [[Video on demand|Video On-Demand]] (VoD), [[Voice over IP]] (VoIP), Audio On-Demand (AoD), [[Dynamic bandwidth allocation|Bandwidth On-Demand]] (BoD), [[Educational technology|remote education]], [[Videotelephony|video conferencing]] services, interactive gaming, and Virtual Private LAN services. BSNL has said that its optic fiber network provides fixed access to deliver high-speed Internet up to 300 Mbit/s.{{cite news|url=https://www.bsnl.co.in/opencms/bsnl/BSNL/services/broadband/ftth_overview.html|title=Bharat Fiber FTTH Overview|date=17 February 2019|publisher=BSNL, LLC}}{{cite news|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/features/story/bsnl-bharat-fiber-ftth-pricing-availability-plans-and-everything-you-need-to-know-1448407-2019-02-05|title=BSNL Bharat Fiber FTTH, Everything you need to know|date=6 February 2019|publisher=[[India Today]]}}{{cite news|url=https://www.bsnltariff.com/2021/05/bsnl-broadband-voip-configuration-for-landline-phone.html|title=BSNL Broadband VOIP Configuration for Landline Phone Instrument|date=31 August 2021|website=Bsnltariff.com}} ==== Bharat Net ==== With effect to the government of India's policy decision to provide state-owned BSNL with another revival package worth 1.64 lakh crore rupees, the struggling PSU was merged with the Government's special purpose vehicle [[Bharat Broadband Network|BBNL]]. This gave the struggling PSU a boost and an additional advantage of an additional 5.67 lakh kilometers of optical fiber, which has been laid across 1.85 lakh village panchayats in the country using the Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF). Currently, it has an optical fibre cable network of over 6.83 lakh kilometres. ====BSNL 4G==== BSNL is the first telecom operator in India to start rolling out 4G service by using Mobile Broadband in 2009. In 2010 BWA auction, BSNL was allocated with 4G spectrum under 2300MHz Bandwidth (in all 20 telecom circles in India except Delhi & Mumbai because it is administered under MTNL network but MTNL also allocated with the same) which is also known as BWA or Broadband Wireless Access spectrum. It is initially used for WiMAX, and later the same is used for LTE service. BSNL was allocated the spectrum without participating in the BWA auction, because it is a state-owned entity, owing to which it has been provided with Auction Exception. So, in order to acquire the spectrum, BSNL has to pay the equivalent amount that private telecom players paid for the same Bandwidth in the Auction to the Government. So, BSNL has provided 8,500 crores to the Government for this spectrum. MTNL also provided 1120 crores to the Government for the same. In the meanwhile other telecom players were using LTE technology to provide 4G services, BSNL alone used WiMAX technology to provide 4G service. But WiMAX technology is not accepted globally due to which the technology got failed to prove. So BSNL returned back all the 4G WiMAX technologies to the Government and brought back the investment amount due to heavy financial debt incurred at the time.{{Cite web |title=BSNL and MTNL to get $1.8B refund for surrendering 4G spectrum |url=https://www.vccircle.com/bsnl-and-mtnl-get-18b-refund-surrendering-4g-spectrum |access-date=2025-02-16 |website=VCCircle |language=en-US}} Reason behind the financial burden is because of its Legacy Systems and increasing pension to retired employees. Later in 2017-18 period BSNL provided 4G services in Few areas of India under Spectrum Reframing despite being not a proper 4G service. Under Make in India initiative, C-DOT ([[Centre for Development of Telematics|Centre for Development of Telemarics]]) developed the 4G core network for India. But the assembly segment was developed by Tejas Network (which was later brought by [[Tata Communications|TATA]]) and the Government owned entity ITI ([[Indian Telephone Industries Limited]]). BSNL started 4G service in some parts of India such as Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh in January 2019, but it is limited to a few cities and towns. Most of its 4G services are currently available in Southern India. However, BSNL is trying to launch pan-India 4G services up to September 2022.{{Cite web|title=BSNL has given September 2022 timeline for pan-India 4G rollout: MoS Telecom - ET Telecom|url=https://telecom.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/bsnl-has-given-september-2022-timeline-for-pan-india-4g-rollout-mos-telecom/88031211|access-date=2021-12-01|website=ETTelecom.com|language=en}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.indiatimes.com/technology/news/bsnl-4g-india-sep-2022-deadline-555804.html|title=Too Soon? BSNL Will Roll Out 4G Services Across India Before September 2022|website=India Times|date= 2 December 2021|access-date=3 December 2021|language= en}} The telecom minister said that BSNL will launch its 4G services all over India on the 75th Independence Day of India along with various other projects.{{Cite web |date=2022-02-22 |title=BSNL & TCS Will Launch 4G On Independence Day? This Is What We Know So Far About BSNL 4G Launch |url=https://trak.in/tags/business/2022/02/22/bsnl-tcs-will-launch-4g-on-independence-day-this-is-what-we-know-so-far-about-bsnl-4g-launch/ |access-date=2022-02-28 |website=Trak.in |language=en-US}} BSNL is using 700 MHz and 2100 MHz bands to roll out the 4G services which can be upgraded to 5G in the future. BSNL has installed more than 40,000 plus 4G enabled and 5G ready towers.{{Cite web |date=2024-12-01 |title=BSNL Has 50,708 4G enabled, 5G-Ready Towers Across India |url=https://aajindia.com/en/tech/bsnl-installing-5g-ready-4g-towers-across-india/ |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=Aaj India |language=en-US}} On September 27, 2025, PM Narendra Modi launched BSNL's Swadeshi 4G Network and commissioned 97500 towers developed indigenously.{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/pm-modi-inaugurates-bsnls-swadeshi-4g-network-commissions-nearly-98000-mobile-4g-towers-from-odisha-2794310-2025-09-27|title=PM unveils BSNL’s swadeshi 4G network, commissions 97,500 towers|date=27 September 2025|website=India Today|access-date=17 July 2026}}{{Cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/infrastructure/indias-swadeshi-4g-push-pm-modi-launches-bsnls-indigenous-services-heres-all-you-need-to-know/articleshow/124179908.cms|title=India's 'swadeshi' 4G push: PM Modi launches BSNL's indigenous services - Here's all you need to know|date=27 September 2025|access-date=17 July 2026|publisher=[[The Economic Times]]}} ====BSNL 5G==== On behalf of the government of India, the Minister of Communications [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]] announced that the State-Owned Telco would start its 5G operations by 15 August 2023. He also added that the 4G and 5G network of the state-owned [[Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited|BSNL]] would be a completely home-grown indigenous 4G and 5G network technology; thus, emphasizing more on Govt. of India's [[Atmanirbhar Bharat]].{{Cite web|title=BSNL to roll out 5G in August 2023: Ashwini Vaishnaw|url=https://www.livemint.com/technology/tech-news/bsnl-to-roll-out-5g-in-august-2023-ashwini-vaishnaw-11664689122465.html|access-date=2022-10-08|website=Livemint.com|date=2 October 2022 |language=en}}{{Cite web|title=TCS set to win $2-billion deal from BSNL for 4G and 5G roll-out|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/tcs-bsnl-deal-to-develop-4g-core-may-take-a-couple-of-months-122100301080_1.html|access-date=2022-10-08|website=Business-standard.com|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=TCS set to win $2-billion deal from BSNL for 4G and 5G roll-out|url=https://www.rediff.com/business/report/tcs-set-to-win-2-billion-deal-from-bsnl-for-4g-and-5g-roll-out/20221004.htm|access-date=2022-10-08|website=Rediff.com|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Going big BSNL set to buy 4G gear from TCS|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/bsnl-set-to-buy-4g-gear-from-tcs/article65967060.ece|access-date=2022-10-08|website=Thehindubusinessline.com|date=3 October 2022 |language=en}} ====Direct-to-Device==== In November 2024, BSNL introduced and made a trial of the new '''Direct-to-Device''' technology for the first time in India in partnership with VIASAT. This technology enables users to communicate without transversing a Base Station or Core Network. This technology is used in direct interaction between [[5G]]-enabled devices to connect seamlessly to both terrestrial and satellite coverage.{{Cite web |date=2024-10-15 |title=Direct-to-device satellite services successfully trialed for first time in India by Viasat and BSNL |url=https://news.viasat.com/newsroom/press-releases/direct-to-device-satellite-services-successfully-trialed-for-first-time-in-india-by-viasat-and-bsnl |access-date=2024-11-09 |website=viasat.com |language=en}} ===IP & cloud services=== ====BSNL Managed Cloud Services==== On 28 May 2013, BSNL launched "Internet Data Centre – Managed Cloud Services". This includes computation, software, data access and storage services for individuals as well as enterprises.{{Cite web |title=Internet Data Center- Managed Cloud Services |url=https://www.bsnl.co.in/opencms/bsnl/BSNL/services/enterprises/managedcloud.html}} Services include: * Cloud compute * Cloud Storage * Hosted Exchange * Hosted Virtual Desktop Infra (VDI) * Hosted Gateway * Hosted Email filter * Hosted web filter * Hosted backup and restore * Hosted DR * Hosted communication Services * Hosted Database ====BSNL Wing Services==== On 16 August 2018, BSNL launched "BSNL Wings Services" in [[Mobile telephone numbering in India|22 telecom circles]], in which there is no need for a [[SIM card]] or [[Fiber to the x|FTTH]] as it is a [[Voice over IP|VoIP]] service through an app.{{cite news|url=https://gadgets.ndtv.com/telecom/news/bsnl-offers-one-month-free-wings-service-to-new-customers-launches-app-in-google-play-store-1987377|title=BSNL offers wings services|date=2 February 2019|publisher=[[NDTV]]}} It offers unlimited free calling for one year throughout India.{{cite web|url=https://www.bsnl.co.in/opencms/bsnl/BSNL/services/landline/wings.html|title=BSNL Wings Services launched in 22 telecom circles|date=29 June 2019|website=BSNL}} ==Administrative units== ===BSNL vertical divisions=== BSNL is primarily divided into three vertical divisions: *BSNL — Consumer Fixed Access (CFA), wire line and broadband business. *BSNL — Consumer Mobility (CM), wireless business, primarily 3G/4G GSM services, WLL-M services. {{Citation |title=WLL-M |url=https://www.bsnl.co.in/opencms/bsnl/BSNL/services/landline/wll.html}} *BSNL — Enterprise Business, Enterprise customers on turnkey basis. Other than these three vertical divisions, there are electrical wings and civil wings, which take care of real estate monetization. ===BSNL horizontal divisions=== Horizontally, BSNL is divided into several administrative units, variously known as telecom circles, metro districts, project circles and specialized units. It has 24 telecom circles, two metro districts, six project circles, four maintenance regions, five telecom factories, three training institutions and four specialized telecom units.{{cite web|url=http://www.bsnl.co.in:9080/opencms/bsnl/BSNL/about_us/bsnl_unit.html|title=BSNL Units|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120906000312/http://www.bsnl.co.in:9080/opencms/bsnl/BSNL/about_us/bsnl_unit.html|archive-date=6 September 2012}} Each circle is headed by a Chief General Manager (CGM) who is an officer of Indian Telecom Service (ITS). The organizational structure of BSNL is as follows: Chief General Manager being the head of the Circle who is the officer of HAG+ level, assisted by three or four Principal General Manager (PGM) who are the officer of grade HAG. The districts over a circle is being headed by the designations as General Manager officer of grade of SAG who looks over around two to four districts, while where the connections are less and the smaller district is being headed by Telecom District Manager (TDM) Officer of the grade of JAG and Telecom Divisional Engineer (TDE) officer of STS grade, all the officers above the post of TDE (including TDE) are of Group A, and they are the officers of grade of Indian Telecom Service (ITS) directly or promotive. Then the Group B consists of Additional Divisional Engineer, Sub Divisional Engineer and Junior Telecom officer and then the organization has Group C and D employees. ==Merger and acquisitions== On 24 October 2019, the Government of India announced a revival package for BSNL and [[Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited|MTNL]] which includes monetizing assets, raising funds, [[LTE (telecommunication)|TD-LTE]] spectrum, and a voluntary retirement scheme for employees. Apart from the package, the [[Ministry of Communications (India)|Ministry of Communications]] has decided to merge MTNL with BSNL. Pending this, MTNL will be a wholly owned [[subsidiary]] of BSNL.{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/policy/bsnl-mtnl-to-be-merged-cabinet-approves-four-way-revival-plan-for-the-two/articleshow/71721833.cms|title=Government approves Revival package for BSNL, MTNL|date=23 October 2019|publisher=[[The Economic Times|Economic Times]]}}{{cite news|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/business/story/bsnl-mtnl-merge-1612281-2019-10-23|title=BSNL, MTNL to be merged, along with special package|date=23 October 2019|publisher=[[India Today]]}}{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/bsnl-mtnl-to-be-merged-centre-lines-up-rs-70000-crore-revival-package/articleshow/71730263.cms|title=BSNL, MTNL to be merged, centre lines up rs 70000 crore revival package|date=29 October 2019|publisher=[[Times of India]]}} On 24 October 2019, the Government of India announced a revival package for BSNL and has given its agreement to an in-principle merger (operational merger, i.e., only the operations of [[Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited|MTNL]] and BSNL would be merged, and they would be managed by BSNL) for MTNL and BSNL{{Cite news |title=BSNL, MTNL to merge under Rs 69,000 cr revival plan, 4G spectrum, VRS part of scheme|work=India Today|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/business/story/bsnl-mtnl-merge-1612281-2019-10-23 |access-date=2022-10-08}} On 27 July 2022, the Government of India announced another revival package for the state-owned BSNL, for providing 4G and 5G services making the [[Public Sector Undertakings in India|PSU]] more viable and vibrant and turning it into a profit making organization; under this policy decision the government also merged [[BBNL]] with BSNL.{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/telecom-news/cabinet-clears-bsnl-bbnl-merger-approves-revival-package-worth-rs-164156-cr/articleshow/93162008.cms |title=Cabinet clears BSNL-BBNL merger, approves revival package worth Rs 1.64 lakh cr |publisher=[[The Economic Times]]}} ==Controversies== ===Website hacking=== In 2012 [[Nikhil Thakur]], a hacker and Internet activist, broke into the Madhya Pradesh BSNL website and later on hacked the India BSNL website.{{Cite web|url=https://www.patheos.com/blogs/drishtikone/2012/11/bsnl-server-vulnerable-to-hacking-shows-a-19-yr-old/|title=BSNL Server Vulnerable To Hacking; Shows A 19 Yr Old|date=12 November 2012}}{{cite news|title=all india bsnl hacked|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/bhopal/19-yr-old-hacks-bsnl-server/article1-956591.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121108230101/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Bhopal/19-yr-old-hacks-BSNL-server/Article1-956591.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 November 2012|newspaper=hindustan times}} ===Cyberattack=== In July 2017, BSNL suffered a cyberattack, in [[Karnataka]], when malware affected the telco's broadband network using modems with default passwords.{{Cite web|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/technology/tech-news-technology/bsnl-asks-net-users-to-change-password-after-malware-attack-4770766/|title=BSNL asks 2000 users to change modem password after malware attack|date=28 July 2018|website=Indian Express|access-date=9 February 2018}} The virus reportedly affected 60,000 modems and blocked their internet connectivity. Later, BSNL issued an advisory notice to its broadband customers, urging them to change their default router username and passwords.{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/karnataka/malware-affects-thousands-of-bsnl-broadband-modems/article19381410.ece|title=Malware affects thousands of BSNL broadband modems |date=17 July 2017|website=The Hindu|access-date=18 November 2021}} == See also == {{Portal|India|Companies}} *[[Government of India]] *[[BSNL Broadband]] *[[BSNL Mobile]] *[[Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited]] *[[Telecommunications in India]] *[[List of telecom companies in India]] *[[List of mobile network operators]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * [http://www.bsnl.co.in Official website] {{Ministry of Communications (India)}} {{Telecommunication companies of India}} {{Public Sector Undertakings in India}} {{Major telecommunications companies}} {{authority control}} [[Category:Government-owned companies of India]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 2000]] [[Category:Companies based in New Delhi]] [[Category:Telecommunications companies of India]] [[Category:Internet service providers of India]] [[Category:Telecommunications companies established in 2000]] [[Category:Government-owned telecommunications companies]] [[Category:2000 establishments in Delhi]] [[Category:BSNL]]
extract: Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (transl. India Telecom Corporation Limited), commonly known as BSNL is an Indian central public sector undertaking, under the ownership of Department of Telecommunications. It was established on 1st October 2000 by the Government of India. It provides mobile voice and internet services through its nationwide telecommunications network across India. It is the largest government-owned-wireless telecommunications service provider in India.
